summary: Client SDK retries align across threads causing HTTP/2 stream exhaustion and long-tail inference latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report sudden long-tail inference latency and intermittent timeouts starting 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Root cause appears to be client SDKs issuing coordinated retry bursts that exhaust per-connection HTTP/2 stream limits at the API gateway, causing effectively serialized requests and elevated p95/p99 latency for affected tenants.

Impact:
- Tabletop Analytics observed 30-40% requests with latency spikes >5s and ~2% timeouts (request-level).
- A subset of other enterprise tenants show similar patterns during peak load windows.
- Errors observed primarily as 429 on gateway, then downstream stalls as clients retry synchronously.

Environment:
- Prod API gateway fronting hosted inference clusters in us-east-1.
- Customer using SDK v1.4.2 via pooled worker threads in their microservice.
- SDK config: maxConnections=6, maxStreamsPerConnection not set (defaults to HTTP/2 peer limits), retries=5, baseBackoffMs=300, exponentialBackoff=true, jitter=false.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Spin up 40 threads each sending concurrent short generation requests (avg 120 tokens) at steady QPS that previously worked.
2) Induce transient upstream 429 (e.g., reduce backend capacity or add artificial throttling).
3) Observe client logs: threads issue retries without jitter, aligned backoff windows.
4) Gateway reports "stream allocation" warnings and 5xx throttling spikes.

Expected behavior:
- SDK should apply randomized jitter to retry windows to avoid synchronized retry storms.
- Gateway should gracefully reject beyond stream capacity with clear guidance and metric tags.

Actual behavior:
- Retries from many client threads align and queue on limited HTTP/2 streams per TCP connection, causing effective serialization of requests and greatly increased request latency.
- Network traces show connection pool fully utilized while application-level concurrency remains waiting for an available stream.

Logs and supporting artifacts:
- Customer attached client-side excerpt: repeated identical retry timestamps across threads (attached in ticket).
- API gateway logs show repeated 429 entries from same tenant between 2026-03-09T18:02:10Z and 18:03:45Z and then a surge of downstream 503s.
- Packet captures indicate many clients reuse few TCP connections (HTTP/2 multiplexing) and attempt new streams past server-permitted limits.

Temporary mitigation suggested to customer:
- Reduce per-process worker threads to keep concurrent streams under 50 while we investigate.
- Patch SDK to enable jitter (workaround patch recommended below).
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-09 18:30 UTC: Customer reported spike.
- 2026-03-09 19:00 UTC: Support confirmed identical retry timestamps in client logs; escalated to infra.
- 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC: SRE reproduced pattern in staging using load script that mimics customer's thread pool.

Findings:
- SDK default retry behavior (v1.4.2) uses deterministic exponential backoff without jitter. With multiple threads initialized at the same time and similar failure timing, retries align.
- API gateway enforces a soft limit on concurrent HTTP/2 streams per connection; when exceeded clients experience stream queuing or resets depending on upstream implementation.
- Many customer deployments reuse a small connection pool (maxConnections=6) across dozens of threads, which forces many logical requests to compete for a small number of physical streams.
- Correlated retries cause brief oversubscription of backend bearer tokens and request queues, amplifying retry storms.

Hypothesis validated by staging run: enabling randomized jitter and increasing maxConnections per process eliminated the synchronized bursts and reduced p99 by ~65% in the experiment.

Next steps planned:
- Backport SDK hotfix to 1.4.x that turns on jitter by default and documents recommended pool sizing for common thread pool sizes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4512 (in review).
- Update SDK docs to include guidance: (1) prefer more connections with lower per-connection streams when client will create many simultaneous goroutines/threads, (2) enable jitter, (3) cap retries for short requests.
- Add gateway metric exposing per-connection stream saturation and a per-tenant tag to help diagnostics.
- Outreach: schedule a 1:1 with Tabletop Analytics to apply temporary config recommended and plan rollout of SDK fix.

resolution:
Workaround and permanent fix applied:
- Short-term: Customer increased maxConnections to 12 and limited worker threads. Observed immediate reduction in timeouts and p99 latency.
- Medium-term: Backported SDK patch to enable randomized jitter by default and added explicit guidance for connection pool sizing for thread-heavy clients (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4512). Backport PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4520.
- Platform: Instrumentation added to gateway to surface per-connection stream saturation (rolled out to prod us-east on 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC).
- Documentation: SDK quickstart updated to include retry/jitter guidance and recommended defaults for enterprise thread pool patterns.

Follow-ups:
- Owner: Priya Rao (SDK) for tracking backport rollout and release notes.
- Owner: Marco Chen (SRE) to monitor gateway stream metrics and add alerting for per-tenant stream saturation.
- Customer follow-up call scheduled and ticket will be closed after 72h of stable metrics.
